heroHeadline: Africa's First Satellite-to-Phone Service Goes Live in DRC as Starlink Tops 11,000 Satellites and 13 Million Subscribers
heroSubtitle: Airtel Africa switched on Starlink Mobile in Kinshasa on August 14, 2026, the continent's first commercial direct-to-phone satellite service, letting ordinary LTE Android handsets reach SMS and WhatsApp with no dish required. Starlink's constellation passed 11,000 satellites on August 19 and SpaceX disclosed over 13 million consumer subscribers in an internal all-hands meeting posted publicly on August 11 — both new highs for the network underpinning much of this year's connectivity growth. The World Bank Group's IFC committed $25 million to Jumia on August 12 to expand digital commerce access for roughly 60,000 African sellers and 100,000+ sales agents. In the US, the National Digital Inclusion Alliance and the Commerce Department agreed August 17 to pause litigation over the terminated Digital Equity Act grant program while NTIA drafts a replacement funding notice targeted for December 2026.
footerNote: Data sourced from ITU, GSMA, World Bank/IFC, A4AI, SpaceX, NTIA/FCC, and major international research outlets. Contested figures noted with confidence levels.
